scope: Current code and production configuration. This is not a guarantee against future vulnerabilities.

controls.evidence: Parameterized PostgreSQL/Oracle values; fixed allowlists and quoted identifiers for dynamic catalog names.
React escaping for application/print content, CSP, nosniff, and frame restrictions.
HttpOnly Strict host cookie, session-bound CSRF proof, and first-party Origin checks; account-security-http.test.mjs.
Scan signature/dimension/size checks; contract attachment type/content allowlist; attachment-security.test.mjs.
Fixed identity/sync destinations and refused credentialed redirects. Private ERP and managed-identity destinations remain intentional administrator-configured integrations.
Existing owner, object, batch and site guards; scan-batch-owner-access.test.mjs and log-book-site-access.test.mjs.
Per-account and socket-peer login throttles, bounded login bodies, ten MFA attempts per account per five minutes.
Salted scrypt retained with malformed-hash rejection. Pulse remains the production primary identity provider.

TOTP with recent primary sign-in for enrollment, replay prevention, one-use recovery, authenticator replacement and session revocation; verify-account-security-browser.mjs. Mandatory enforcement was disabled by the newer sign-in compatibility release.
Existing deny-by-default permissions remain; new security endpoints expose only self-service operations.

Forced restrictive site RLS for operational log books and their views; transaction-local HTTP scopes, explicit trusted-job separation, row-security.test.mjs. Scan objects retain existing server owner/site authorization.
MIS uses opaque server-side session IDs rather than browser JWT authentication.
Server-side AES-GCM integration secrets and a separate Key Vault credential for the restricted MIS database role.

Tab-isolated HttpOnly credentials; only profile data and a non-secret context marker remain in browser storage. Legacy sessions rotate and old credentials are invalidated. PC-scanner credentials remain scoped and expiring.
Random dedicated database credential; no new default MIS password. Production trusts Pulse. Shared administrator and Pulse passwords are preserved.
No wildcard application CORS. Cookie mutations require the MIS origin; PC connector access retains exact loopback/host/header checks.
Telegram secret verification precedes message processing; authenticated machine integrations remain separate from browser MFA.
Private paths and source maps are blocked; static fallback serves only public assets; http-security.test.mjs.
Query sign-in codes, rejected parser bodies, credential URLs, MFA/recovery material and secret fields are excluded or redacted.
Patched sharp override; zero known dependency audit findings; real Transformers PNG/JPEG/WebP preprocessing compatibility test.
MIS role cannot create databases/roles or bypass RLS. Real PostgreSQL test confirms it cannot read a separate application's tables.
Production requires isolated database mode and RLS. HTTP database access waits for successful RLS initialization.

userAction: At the next sign-in, enroll an authenticator and save the recovery codes. Old sessions may require a fresh Pulse sign-in before enrollment.
